tasks.title: completionGate race: stale resolveGate settle after collective switch corrupts the membership SSOT
tasks.redPrompt:
RED for #260 (rules: _shared of teams/mvox-dev/memory/pipeline-args/args-260.json — read it first; the issue's done-when governs). One defect, surgical fix.

THE DEFECT (triage-verified): profile/+page.svelte ~:383-390 (pre-batch-B numbering — re-grep) does resolveGate(...).then(state => completionGateStore.set(state)) with NO generation guard. completionGateStore is the app-wide SSOT for membership-in-good-standing — its contract is that no surface re-derives it, so a stale write opens the hole everywhere at once and BY DESIGN nothing downstream can catch it (the value is keyed to nothing). Failure: resolve starts for collective A, user switches to B, A's read settles late → stale 'complete' suppresses the /profile redirect and re-enables member affordances app-wide.

THE PROOF CLAUSE — THIS IS WHAT REVIEW GATES ON (Bentham, standing reviewer, pre-committed): a timing race resists commit-replay — a test that fails pre-fix by scheduling accident proves nothing and may pass on a fast run. The regression test MUST be DETERMINISTICALLY ORDERED: hold the resolveGate promise manually (deferred/controlled promise in the mock), switch collectives, THEN settle the stale read — a construction that fails against pre-fix code EVERY time and passes post-fix EVERY time. And it must fail FOR THE RIGHT REASON: the assertion that trips must show the stale 'complete' actually reaching completionGateStore (assert the store's value), not a timeout or an unrelated assertion. Run it against current main and REPORT THE FAILURE OUTPUT verbatim (#253 standard — the failure evidence, not a green suite).

ALSO PIN: (1) the guarded path — A's late settle after a switch to B leaves the store on B's state (or the loading state pending B's resolve), never A's; (2) the happy path unchanged — same-collective resolve still lands normally; (3) rapid A→B→A: only the LAST requested context's result lands (the guard must key on request generation or collective identity, GREEN's choice — RED asserts outcome, not mechanism); (4) a REJECTED stale read after a switch is also ignored (no stale error state from a context the user left); (5) the store's consumers are untouched — this is a write-side guard, no API change (pin the store's exported shape).

HOUSE PRECEDENT to mirror, not reinvent: the event page's generation guards (:300/:430/:569 family, re-grep) and #255's call-time capture pattern (isPastDetail capture — same family, per-request context captured at initiation and compared at settle). Scope fence: profile page gate wiring only — resolveGate's internals, completionGate consumers, membership store from #255, and anything else on the page are OFF-LIMITS unless the guard structurally requires a seam (justify any touch).

tasks.commitBody:
resolveGate's settle wrote completionGateStore unguarded: start a
resolve for collective A, switch to B, and A's late answer landed
as the current truth. completionGate is the app-wide single source
of truth for membership in good standing — its contract is that no
surface re-derives it, which is exactly why a stale write opened
the hole everywhere at once and nothing downstream was positioned
to catch it: the written value is keyed to nothing. A stale
'complete' suppressed the /profile redirect and re-enabled member
affordances app-wide.

The fix is the house generation-guard idiom: the request context
is captured when a resolve is initiated and compared at settle; a
settle from a context the user has left writes nothing — neither
value nor error. Rapid switching leaves only the last-requested
context's result. The store's shape and every consumer are
untouched; this is a write-side guard.

The regression test is deterministically ordered — the resolve
promise is held, the collective switched, then the stale read
settled — so it fails against the pre-fix code every run, for the
right reason (the stale 'complete' reaching the store), and cannot
pass by scheduling accident. Its pre-fix failure output is in the
review record, per the standard set on #253: a regression test
that passes before the fix is not testing the fix, and a timing
test that fails by accident is not failing at all.

This closes the audit #260 documented: a standing stand-down
whose 'single-collective, no picker' premise went stale when
multi-collective shipped. The other two findings closed under that
premise were adjudicated on the issue — one unreachable, one with
no observable effect.

Live gate (Mihkel): with two collectives, open /profile in A,
switch to B mid-load, and the gate banner reflects B — never A's
leftover answer.
